context: Interactive nutrient treemap explorer with a zoomable treemap (area encodes calories by food group) linked to a parallel coordinates plot (6 nutritional dims: calories, protein, fat, carbs, fiber, sugar) with brushable axes for cross-filtering.
first_impression: Structurally honest dual-view visualization with correct area encoding and data-driven scales throughout.
what_works: Treemap correctly uses .sum(d => d.calories) mapping calorie values directly to rectangular area — no lie factor. Parallel coordinates builds per-dimension scales via d3.extent(leaves, d => d.data[dim]) rather than hardcoded domains, making them fully data-driven and robust to data changes.
what_doesnt: Brush filter logic compares pixel-space coordinates (scales[dim](d.data[dim]) >= y0) which is correct but couples filter correctness to scale stability — if setupParcoords() were called mid-brush it would silently reset filters. The parallel coordinates domain starts at the data minimum rather than zero, which is standard and correct for this chart type but means absolute magnitude is not visually apparent across axes with very different ranges (e.g., calories 15–717 vs fiber 0–34.4 share no common visual anchor).
